newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: U.N. recommends six-month renewal of Macedonia force.
newsitem.headline: U.N. recommends six-month renewal of Macedonia force.

text.p: Secretary-General Kofi Annan on Wednesday recommended a six-month renewal, until November 30, of the 1,050-strong U.N. force in the former Yugoslav republic of Macedonia.
In a written report to the Security Council, he said the unsettled situation in neighbouring Albania ruled out ending or reducing the mission now.
But he said it might be possible to begin a phased reduction of 300 troops after four months, depending on the situation at the time.
The U.N. Preventive Deployment Force (UNPREDP), as it is called, was originally deployed to prevent conflicts elsewhere in the former Yugoslavia from spilling over into Macedonia.
It includes nearly 500 United States troops, similar-sized contingents from Finland, Denmark, Norway and Sweden, and about 50 soldiers from Indonesia.

When the Security Council last November renewed UNPREDEP's mandate until May 31 it also called for a phased 300-man reduction, to be completed by April 30. But on April 9 the council suspended the drawdown because of unrest in Albania.
Annan said in his latest report that recent developments in Albania "have demonstrated that stability in the Balkan region remains extremely fragile."
It would be "imprudent to recommend that the UNPREDEP mission be terminated" and "equally imprudent to recommend any immediate changes in the mandate or size of the force at this time," he said.
"I therefore recommend that the mandate of UNPREDEP be renewed for an additional six months until November 30, 1997."

He said he also recommended that the present strength of the force be maintained up to September 30, 1997, "with a view to starting as of October 1, 1997...a two-month phased reduction of the military component to the 750 troop level foreseen by the council in resolution 1082 (1996)," he added, referring to last November's planned cut.

Citing doubts about the possibility of holding free and fair elections in Albania in June, Annan said the absence of a legitimate, elected and representative government and of progress in rebuilding public institutions would undermine efforts to revive the shattered economy.

A 6,350-strong U.N.-authorised force under Italian command is currently deployed in Albania to help protect relief supplies amid chaos that followed the collapse this year of several get-rich-quick "pyramid" schemes in which many Albanians lost their savings.
Annan said the "lack of a perceptible and early change in the situation in Albania could lead to another explosion of internal violence," which might affect neighbouring countries.

He said the large number of weapons circulating in the region posed a risk to stability, adding that "yet another potentially destabilising factor in the coming months will be the outcome of the elections scheduled to be held in Bosnia and Herzegovina in September of this year."
